guard_streams.source: Ofcom simpler and quicker broadband switching guide

facts.detail: Residential broadband and landline customers using One Touch Switch contact only their new provider.
The current provider automatically supplies switching information including early-termination charges and effects on other services.
Customers must not pay notice-period charges beyond the switch date.
Providers must compensate customers when switch failures leave them without service for more than one working day.

guard_streams.write_limit: Switching workflow and compensation evidence do not establish parcel network availability or performance.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom mobile switching and number porting guide

facts.detail: Customers keeping a mobile number request a Porting Authorisation Code and give it to the new provider.
A PAC remains valid for 30 days and can be requested again after expiry.
After the PAC is supplied, the number should normally be ready on the new service within one working day.
Customers not keeping their number use a Service Termination Authorisation Code instead.

guard_streams.write_limit: PAC, STAC and port timing do not prove radio coverage or fixed broadband availability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom mobile switching and number porting guide

facts.detail: Mobile providers cannot charge notice periods running after the switch date.
A switch taking more than one working day can create entitlement to reasonable compensation.
Reasonable compensation also applies where the provider abuses the switching process.
A customer may request free number retention from the new provider within one month after cancelling the old service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile switching remedies are customer-account evidence, not parcel signal measurement.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom changing provider complaint and porting guide

facts.detail: Phone providers must allow customers to take their telephone number when switching.
A customer who believes porting is blocked or delayed should contact the new provider.
An independent industry panel can assess a case and override the old provider to complete porting.
Providers must offer compensation and explain how to claim when they block or delay number porting.

guard_streams.write_limit: Porting investigations and remedies cannot populate parcel coverage, technology or speed fields.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom General Conditions protecting business customers

facts.detail: Protected business customers must receive adequate switching information, including compensation rights.
Number porting must be provided on reasonable terms and conditions.
Customers retain the right to port their number for at least one month after switching.
Customers must not be charged directly for porting their number.

guard_streams.write_limit: Business switching protections are regulatory obligations, not parcel-level network evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom General Conditions protecting business customers

facts.detail: If number porting fails, the number and relevant services must be reactivated until completion.
For covered small-business bundles, switching loss of service must not exceed one working day unless technically infeasible.
Key contract information and a one-page, or three-page bundled, summary are required before consent.
Providers must operate compliant complaints procedures and belong to an Ofcom-approved ADR scheme.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract documents, continuity duties and ADR membership do not prove parcel orderability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom locked-handset bundle and accessible-format rules

facts.detail: Mobile companies are prohibited from selling locked handsets.
Rules limiting phone and broadband contracts to two years also cover bundles.
Adding a service cannot extend existing service contract periods without customer consent.
Disabled customers can request important non-marketing service information in a reasonably acceptable accessible format at no extra cost.

guard_streams.write_limit: Handset, bundle and accessibility protections do not establish network coverage.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom One Touch Switch enforcement programme

facts.detail: Ofcom opened an industry-wide One Touch Switch enforcement programme on 3 April 2023.
The programme followed industry's failure to implement the process by that deadline.
General Conditions C7.18 to C7.27 specify the residential One Touch Switch process.
Providers must offer residential fixed-line and broadband customers one switching process free of charge.

guard_streams.write_limit: An enforcement programme and legal scope do not identify current parcel serviceability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Cheshire contract termination and Openreach reassignment

facts.detail: BDUK and Freedom Fibre mutually terminated the Cheshire Project Gigabit contract.
Freedom Fibre received no public funding for that terminated contract.
In February 2026 Cheshire premises were moved into Openreach call-off eight.
Call-off eight provides £37.5 million for around 18,500 hard-to-reach Cheshire premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Termination and replacement procurement do not prove that an individual premise has been built or connected.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract termination

facts.detail: CityFibre is no longer delivering the Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract.
BDUK and CityFibre mutually agreed to end the contract.
Expanded commercial rollout and market conditions reduced the need for public funding.
BDUK is discussing alternatives for the few premises not covered by other rollout plans.

guard_streams.write_limit: Commercial rollout and contract termination cannot be converted into exact parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Derbyshire Peak District contract reassignment

facts.detail: FullFibre is no longer delivering the Peak District contract.
BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate the contract.
BDUK stated it was putting alternative supplier plans in place.
In April 2026 the Peak District area was added to Openreach call-off one covering parts of Staffordshire.

guard_streams.write_limit: Reassignment changes the delivery route but does not prove live address-level service.

guard_streams.source: BDUK West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract reassignment

facts.detail: BDUK and FullFibre mutually terminated the West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract.
BDUK stated it was moving to alternative plans with other suppliers.
West Herefordshire was added to Openreach call-off three in April 2026.
The published call-off-three change explicitly names West Herefordshire, not the full former contract geography.

guard_streams.write_limit: Partial geographic reassignment must not be interpreted as delivery for every premise in the former contract.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Kent and Cambridgeshire contract redesigns

facts.detail: Kent was redesigned in May 2026 to around 9,000 premises with £26.1 million investment.
Kent's original CityFibre contract covered around 50,000 premises with a £112 million value.
Cambridgeshire was redesigned to around 35,000 premises backed by up to £77 million.
The original Cambridgeshire contract targeted up to 45,000 premises with a £69 million value.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesigned and original contract scopes are planning evidence, not current parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK July 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress

facts.detail: The July management table includes initial-scope contracted premises and may exclude deferred scope.
It is a 16 July 2026 snapshot subject to variable ingestion lag and must not assess milestones.
The table reports CO8 Cheshire at 18,460 contracted and zero built, and Kent at 8,750 contracted and 2,530 built.
The rounded table total is 838,490 contracted and 287,510 built contracted premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded management information is not directly comparable with official statistics and cannot identify exact parcel delivery.

guard_streams.source: Canonical slot state and exact-output acceptance

facts.detail: Canonical continuation and runtime records show no live owner.
No active or over-15-minute PENDING execution exists.
The legacy heartbeat path remains absent; terminal continuation and runtime records remain the ownership fallback.
No candidate, measured-speed row or accuracy promotion is allowed before accepted r2 bytes, exact join and hardened postjoin readback.

guard_streams.write_limit: Final completion still requires the canonical Windows-host archive and postjoin evidence.
